title: Summarising
examples: How do I know what the most important part is?
Should I use my own words when I summarise?
Is there a good way to count the words?

explain.say: Today we are learning to summarise what we read.

items: Say what the text is about.
Pick only the most important ideas.
Write it in your own words.

explain.say: First, you must find the main idea of the whole text.

draw.text: Main Idea: What is it about?

explain.say: Next, you should find the key points that support that main idea.
Remember to write everything using your own words.
A good summary keeps a very tight word limit.
For example, if the text is about dogs, your summary should only say that.

faq.q: How many words should my summary be?
faq.a: There is no exact number, but you must keep it much shorter than the original text. Try to aim for a specific word count if your teacher gives one.
asks: Should I write a paragraph or just a few sentences?
Is there a rule for the word count?

faq.q: Do I have to use my own words?
faq.a: Yes, you must use your own words. This shows you understood the meaning, not just copied it.
asks: Can I just change a few words?
Is paraphrasing the same as using my own words?

faq.q: What is the main idea if the text has many parts?
faq.a: Read through everything and ask yourself what the text is mostly about. That is usually the main idea.
asks: How do I find the main point?

faq.q: Should I include all the examples from the text?
faq.a: No, you should only include the key points. Examples are details, not the main message.
asks: Are examples important in a summary?
Should I leave out the supporting facts?

faq.q: What if I don't understand the text well?
faq.a: It is okay to ask for help. Try reading the text a couple of times to help you understand it better first.
asks: What if the text is too hard?
Can I summarise if I am confused?

facts: A summary tells the main points of a text.
You must write the summary in your own words.
A summary must be much shorter than the original reading.
The main idea is the most important message.

quiz.say: A text is about recycling plastic bottles and how to sort them correctly. Which sentence is the best summary?
quiz.show: A. Plastic bottles are useful for many things.

options.show: B. Recycling plastic bottles requires sorting them into different types.
options.say: B. Recycling plastic bottles requires sorting them into different types.

options.show: A. Plastic bottles are useful for many things.
options.say: A. Plastic bottles are useful for many things.

options.show: C. You must wash the bottles before you put them in the bin.
options.say: C. You must wash the bottles before you put them in the bin.

options.show: D. There are many types of plastic bottles to recycle.
options.say: D. There are many types of plastic bottles to recycle.

quiz.why: This option covers the main action and the key requirement of the text.

wrong.1: This is too general and misses the important part about sorting.
wrong.2: This is just one small detail, not the main idea.
wrong.3: This only talks about the types, not the process of recycling.

quiz.say: If the main idea is 'Healthy eating helps your body grow strong', which key point would fit best?
quiz.show: Key Point: Supporting the main idea

options.show: I should eat apples every day.
options.say: I should eat apples every day.

quiz.why: This fact directly supports the idea that healthy eating is good for the body.

wrong.1: This is too specific and sounds like a rule, not a general point.
wrong.2: This is completely unrelated to the topic of healthy eating.
wrong.3: This is an observation about the weather, not the text's topic.

quiz.say: A text describes the life cycle of a butterfly. What is the main idea?

options.show: The butterfly eats leaves when it is a caterpillar.
options.say: The butterfly eats leaves when it is a caterpillar.

options.show: It needs time to grow big.
options.say: It needs time to grow big.

options.show: The butterfly goes through four distinct stages.
options.say: The butterfly goes through four distinct stages.

quiz.why: This captures the entire process shown in the cycle diagram.

wrong.0: This is only one stage, not the whole cycle.
wrong.1: This is just a description, not the main idea of the life cycle.
wrong.2: This is true but too vague to be the main idea.
